claim: Human bio-inspired design starts from either end: problem-driven (reframe the problem in biological terms, then search) or solution-based (start from a biological solution, then look for a problem). Solution-based work is common (4/9 and 5/10 course projects; 27/74 cases, 36.5%).
agent_test: Give the agent two retrieval entry points (problem-to-source, source-to-problem) and compare yield at equal tokens.

claim: Reframing the problem in abstract, biology-ready function terms is the step that opens retrieval ('stopping a bullet' became 'prevent, withstand, heal damage').
agent_test: Retrieve with raw problem text vs a function-abstracted rewrite; score relevant analogues in top 10.

claim: Solution-based (source-first) designs are much more often multifunctional than problem-driven ones (22/27, 81.5% vs 14/47, 29.8%; Fisher p<0.001).
agent_test: Descriptive only; test whether source-first prompts yield more multi-constraint designs on the same tasks.

claim: Fixation on a biological source is common (50/74 cases) but NOT associated with solution-based vs problem-driven design (70.4% vs 66%, n.s.); the earlier claim that source-first causes fixation did not replicate in the 2021 meta-analysis.
agent_test: Measure fixation (same-source repeats) in agent runs started source-first vs problem-first; expect no gap.

claim: Compound analogies (several sources combined) are frequent in human bio-inspired design (6/9 in 2006, 4/10 in 2008 course teams) and link to problem-driven design.
agent_test: Allow the agent to hold 2-3 sources and merge; compare with single-source at equal tokens.

claim: Unaided people rarely retrieve structurally matching analogues: surface-similar stories are retrieved far more than higher-order matches (surface 61.9% vs 11.6%; higher-order 11.9% in the story cue contrast; Exp 2 higher-order 37.3% vs 10.8%).
agent_test: Test the agent's retrieval of surface vs structural matches in a mixed story bank.

claim: A hint to use an analogy raises human solving only modestly in strategy tasks (HR problem 20.3% to 37%; factory 6.3% to 8.7%); the Gick-Holyoak hint effect (29% to 50%) points the same way.
agent_test: Compare agent solve rate with and without an explicit 'use an analogy' instruction.

claim: Far-field examples help novelty only when also uncommon: far+less-common gave mean novelty d=1.14 and max novelty d=1.29 vs control; far alone or less-common alone did not differ from control (N=153).
agent_test: Feed the agent near/far x common/rare examples; score novelty and feasibility at equal tokens. One human lab study carries the interaction.
gap_note: Gap search: Chan 2011 full text re-opened; d values confirmed (far+less-common mean novelty d=1.14, breadth d=-1.03). Table 1 cells sum to 151, not 153; N to be checked.

claim: Far analogies raise variability of quality (d=0.64 vs near, d=0.78 vs control) and cut idea quantity (d=-0.30); more-common examples narrow breadth (d=-1.03 vs control).
agent_test: Track both mean and variance of idea quality under far stimuli; add a filter step after far retrieval.
gap_note: Gap search: confirmed in full text (variability of quality far vs near d=0.64, vs control 0.78; quantity d=-0.30; breadth more-common vs control d=-1.03). Mean and max quality unchanged.

claim: Mid-session near or far stimuli did not change novelty (n=20 per group); near raised feasibility change (d=0.5), far lowered usefulness (d=1.1). Stimulus innovation correlates with outcome innovation (r=0.67).
agent_test: Inject stimuli mid-run; far for divergence early, near for repair late. Test the timing.

claim: Purpose-based (function-only) representation retrieves cross-domain product analogies better than TF-IDF and embeddings (top-1% precision 0.739 vs 0.63); retrieved analogies gave good ideas with p=0.71 vs 0.28 (TF-IDF) vs 0.27 (random), 38 workers, 749 ideas.
agent_test: Index the agent's memory by abstracted purpose/function, not surface text; compare recall of true analogues. Later work (K12) supports the direction.

claim: Domain-stripped or function-focused representations improve cross-domain retrieval: skeleton raised AP 0.222 to 0.513 (18 method families); BARCODE strategy-sentence precision 72% vs 36% at top 7.
agent_test: Rewrite stored items as domain-free skeletons before embedding; compare retrieval AP.

claim: Generic embeddings are weak at cross-domain analogy retrieval; best of 11 retrievers reaches Recall@10 0.26; an LLM reranker reaches 0.81; fine-tuning on analogy pairs lifts to 0.70; HyDE-style rewriting 0.16 to 0.44.
agent_test: Two-stage retrieval: cheap candidate pull, then LLM rerank on structure. Measure recall and token cost.
gap_note: Gap search: 0.81 reranker figure holds only if the positive is in the 151-candidate pool; RATIO shows first-stage recall in top 100 caps the rerank (57-81%).

claim: LLMs match humans on short analogy selection but fall behind as stories lengthen: AnaloBench T1 GPT-4 89.1/66.5/60.7 vs human 96.0/72.5/73.3 (1/10/30 sentences), gaps 6.9/6.0/12.6. The paper's text says 28.8 at 30 sentences; its own tables give 12.6 (text error confirmed by re-reading).
agent_test: Test with long, noisy source descriptions; add a compress-then-match step.
gap_note: Gap search: 28.8 confirmed as an internal error. Table 4 (true-positive subset) gives GPT-4 22.7 at 30 sentences, which is unstable and not to be cited.

claim: LLMs are near chance at retrieving analogues from a story bank (AnaloBench T2, 200+ stories) and at StoryAnalogy choice (ChatGPT ~30%, davinci-003 37.1% vs human 85.7%), even though they do better when mapping a given pair.
agent_test: Do not trust the model to find its own analogues from raw memory; use external retrieval plus rerank.
gap_note: Gap search: T2 GPT-4-Turbo P@3 42.9/6.5/3.9 vs random 3.9; no 2025-2026 model result found.

claim: GPT-4 used the radiation analogy only 1/15 times unprompted (Dolphin 14/15, a near-surface match), yet reached recall 1.00 with a hint (precision ~0.52): models fail to retrieve spontaneously but map well when told to.
agent_test: A trigger step ('list candidate analogous problems') before solving; compare with no trigger.

claim: Emergent analogical reasoning exists in LLMs on standard tasks (GPT-3 above average SAT; GPT-4 near-perfect near analogies) and survives counterfactual tests only in part: GPT-4 worse than humans on altered alphabets (p=8.9e-13) but on par with code execution (p=0.496).
agent_test: Evaluate on altered or counterfactual variants and with tool use so performance is not memorised.

claim: Prompting a model to recall its own relevant problems before solving gives modest gains: Yasunaga et al. report GSM8K GPT-3.5-turbo 75.0 to 77.8 (+1.1 over 5-shot CoT 76.7), text-davinci-003 14.8 (0-shot) to 61.0, PaLM2 60.8 to 81.7; Codeforces Acc@1 GPT-4 16 to 19. Gains are large for weak models only. Replication with irrelevant examples (Qin 2024) finds relevance does not matter on math and the relevant arm can be worse (GSM8K 71.5 vs 75.5); example accuracy drives the effect.
agent_test: Run self-generated exemplars vs fixed few-shot at equal tokens; expect small gains for strong models.
gap_note: Gap search: row labels decoded, 14.8% is the 0-shot row. Qin 2024 shows irrelevant self-generated examples match or beat relevant ones on math. Gwak 2026 shows the gain is a within-prompt process effect (GPT-4.1 GSM8K 48.8 to 57.9 without CoT) and about 1 point with CoT.

claim: LLM-generated analogies are judged meaningful at scale-dependent rates (175B: 70.05% target-only vs human 66.67%); small models mostly fail.
agent_test: Check generated analogies with a judge before use; accept only if the rubric passes.

claim: LLMs as inspiration generators help designers (median helpfulness 4/5; problem reformulation in 80%) but up to 25% of outputs are potentially harmful and concept sets are less diverse than crowds unless prompted.
agent_test: Add a diversity instruction and a harm/irrelevance filter in the analogy step.
gap_note: Gap search: BioSpark (N=12) raised novelty 3.9 to 7.1 and value 3.8 to 7.0 but feasibility fell 6.8 to 5.7.

claim: Fine-tuned or retrieval-grounded LLMs for bio-inspired design produce usable concepts but classifier filters pass only 58-84% and birds dominate (>50% of analogues); structure-level evaluation is weak.
agent_test: Penalise repeated source categories; sample sources across taxa.
gap_note: Gap search: Zhu 2022 human feasibility check covers about 6 generated concepts and 9 raters; no pass rate exists.

claim: Lookup of biology is expensive for humans (40-100 h per organism description; 3.36% of 3,416 articles gave design insight; ~3 person-hours per relevant article), so automated retrieval has real headroom.
agent_test: Report agent cost per relevant analogue found as the main efficiency metric.

claim: Cross-domain science retrieval with LLM agents (Idea-Catalyst) improves novelty +21% and insightfulness +16% over dual retrieval, but human check N=6 and judges are LLMs.
agent_test: Replicate with blind human or independent judges at equal tokens.

claim: TRIZ-style LLM pipelines are only moderately accurate: AutoTRIZ matched 7/10 textbook cases; TRIZ-GPT few-shot lowered recall (0.675 to 0.245) while raising precision.
agent_test: Prefer zero-shot or CoT for contradiction detection; test few-shot only with measured recall.

claim: Mapping a given analogy is easier for LLMs than finding one; on ARCANA hard abstraction tasks the best model is about 48-51% vs humans 58-69%, with large spread between models.
agent_test: Separate tests for retrieval and mapping in the agent; report each.

claim: Explicit analogy generation (2 calls) beats a plain prompt (1 call) and a 'search other domains' prompt (2 calls) on diversity and novelty for Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Flash: binary novelty 50.4/58.8/68.9% vs 21.6/28.2/37.8% (cross-domain) vs 1.6/9.0/8.9% (plain); humans judged AR more novel 78% of the time. No correctness or feasibility measure, and no best-of-N control.
agent_test: Run explicit analogy vs best-of-N at equal tokens, scoring feasibility with a blind judge.

claim: LLMs show source-domain homogeneity in analogy generation, an LLM version of source-locking: baselines produce about 5% unique domains (7-8 of 150); Gemini 3.1 Pro with a diversity prompt reaches only 0.49 intra-output diversity; diversity tricks cost quality (Mistral-7B quality 4.32 to 4.21 for diversity 0.33 to 0.53).
agent_test: Keep a ledger of source domains used and force a different domain on the second pass; count same-source repeats.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Structured decomposition before retrieval helps analogy finding, but for a strong model a plain summary step gets most of it (Sonnet-4.6 MDS: direct 2.24, summary 3.91, self-reflection 4.11, structural decomposition 4.17; 15 events, LLM judge). Deep-research agents with frontier backbones mostly match surface features.
agent_test: Compare summary-only vs structure-only vs both at equal tokens on a design bank.

claim: A retrieve-then-rerank pipeline is bounded by first-stage recall: LLM reranker reaches Recall@10 0.81 on a 151-candidate pool (best embedding 0.26; HyDE 0.44); on a 404k-sentence pool the tuned retriever has the gold item in its top 100 for only 57-81% of queries, and the reranker then keeps it in the top 10 for 72-87%.
agent_test: Widen the first stage (top 100+) and spend the LLM tokens on reranking, not on query rewriting.

claim: Generative AI repeats itself in design: ChatGPT chair concepts had 67.4% unique terms vs 78.2% for award-winning human designs; 7/10 designers noticed repetition (N=10). No test yet of bio-inspired design or of a forced second source.
agent_test: Measure same-source repeats across 20 runs with and without a forced second, different source.

claim: Raising novelty costs feasibility in bio-inspired design with LLM support: BioSpark (N=12, blind expert ratings) novelty 3.9 to 7.1, value 3.8 to 7.0, feasibility 6.8 to 5.7; unique species 4.6 to 8.2; ideas 5.5 to 10.3.
agent_test: Add a feasibility critic after the novelty step; track pass rate and failure reasons.

claim: Where a source becomes too far depends on how similarity is measured: computed boundaries lie at greater distance for visual than for functional similarity (N=36 abstract). The primary near/far sweet-spot figures from Fu 2013, Linsey 2012 and Christensen and Schunn 2007 could not be obtained.
agent_test: Measure distance on function, not appearance; do not cite a numeric sweet spot.
